newsitem.title: USA: Ill. seeks income tax rebates from neighbors-paper.
newsitem.headline: Ill. seeks income tax rebates from neighbors-paper.

text.p: Illinois will seek to recoup as much as $55 million of income taxes from neighboring states whose residents commute across the border from Wisconsin and Indiana, the Chicago Sun-Times reported Friday.

Illinois Revenue Director Kenneth Zehnder has given the states the option of rebating the taxes they get from residents working in Illinois or informing workers they must begin paying the Illinois income tax next year, the newspaper said.
The Illinois General Assembly must still approve legislation allowing the practice, the newspaper said.

Illinois has had reciprocal tax arrangements with Indiana and Wisconsin since the 1970s that allow residents to file a single income tax form in their home state on the assumption that there are an equal number of commuters crossing the borders.
Wisconsin paid Minnesota a $31.8 miillion rebate in 1996 for workers who live in western Wisconsin, but work across the St. Croix River in Minnesota, the newspaper said.
